Examination of the holotype and its comparison with species of Agathocles and Caystrus revealed that it markedly differs from the first genus and fits well the second one, especially in having the body short, more regularly oval and relatively flat, head relatively short, mandibular plates not expanded forward and strongly narrowing anteriad, pronotum with sharp margins, and pale brown dorsal colouration with longitudinal yellowish unpunctured lines along corial veins (cf. Figs 125 – 126). Therefore, we transfer this species to the genus Caystrus, resulting in a new combination: Caystrus dubius (Distant, 1921), comb. nov. We did not find any important differences between C. dubius and C. obscurus, but we leave the decision on their synonymy for a furure revision of Caystrus.

d.a: Distribution and habitat. This species is only known from the type locality, Unnamed Cave 4 (Figs 1 K, 42 A – E), which is located about 0.8 km northwest of Laoshanyaowanggu (a valley near the border between China and Vietnam). The cave was found near the top of a mountain. Several boulders were scattered around the triangular entrance (about 2 meters high and 3 meters wide). The interior space is large, and extends horizontally. The total length of the cave is unknown. All specimens were collected under stones and detritus in the deep zone (temperature around 11 ° C, humidity over 85 %).
